title: The shape of a fork/join step

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what is wrong with a task that calls `left.fork()` and `right.fork()` and then returns `left.join() + right.join()`?

options.text: Each split pays for an extra push and pop through the thread's deque
options.says: The page's Q4 says every split pays for an extra push/pop through the deque and the work is no longer done directly.

options.text: Each split makes the pool add a thread to run tasks during the wait
options.says: The page's Q4 says a waiting ForkJoinPool worker usually runs or helps with the queued tasks itself, so no extra thread is needed.

options.text: Each split leaves its forked tasks queued until the current thread returns
options.says: The page says the waiting worker runs or helps with the queued tasks itself, and idle threads steal tasks from busy threads' deques.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, how do Java 21's virtual threads relate to the Fork/Join framework?

options.text: They replace Fork/Join for CPU-bound decomposition, which is why ForkJoinPool gained close()
options.says: The page says Fork/Join remains the tool of choice for CPU-bound parallel decomposition; close() is listed as a Java 19 addition for try-with-resources.

options.text: They complement it: virtual threads suit I/O-bound tasks and Fork/Join suits CPU-bound work
options.says: The page says virtual threads are better suited for I/O-bound tasks, Fork/Join remains the tool for CPU-bound decomposition, and the two are complementary.

options.text: They run inside it: since Java 21 every fork() starts the subtask on a new virtual thread
options.says: The page describes forked subtasks going to a worker's deque in the ForkJoinPool; it says nothing of fork() starting virtual threads.

concepts: Fork/Join is the tool for CPU-bound decomposition, and virtual threads are the tool for I/O-bound concurrency.
Forking both subtasks and joining both costs an extra fork per split and leaves the current thread only waiting in join.
